title: Memory and code intelligence for agents
subtitle: Agents that remember across sessions and explain code without inventing it

lede: Coding agents forget everything between sessions, rediscover the same facts about a codebase daily, and explain call paths that do not exist with complete confidence. I built the memory and code-intelligence service every agent in my estate connects to. Dependency tracing is a graph query, and the code explainer narrates only edges the graph has proven and refuses when coverage is incomplete. Start with A code explainer that is not allowed to invent. Session memory captures every tool call, extracts what matters, and re-injects it later.
quote: A refusal beats a plausible guess, because the caveat is the first thing a reader stops seeing.
evidence: Code intelligence for AI agents: a tree-sitter code graph covering 294,033 of 294,362 code chunks, with dependency tracing as a bounded database traversal and 0 models involved.
Evidence-grounded LLM output: a code explainer that narrates only edges the graph has proven and returns coverage incomplete, with no free-form fallback.
Persistent agent memory: session memory that captures every tool call as an observation, extracts and embeds it, and re-injects it into later sessions.
Retrieval system design: code, past decisions and reference documents as 3 indexes behind one retrieval surface.
author: Corey James
